title: Common-stage descent of a normalized isomorphism transport family
statement: Fix a prime l, an algebraic closure Ω/Q_l, an isomorphism g:X→Y of noetherian schemes of finite Krull dimension with l invertible, and stalk-unit proofs hX,hY. For every small finite coefficient field E in Ω suppose given normalized stages S_E for g and R_E for inv g, in the sense of [def-pod-isomorphism-field-transport-clauses]. Suppose both families obey isomorphismFieldTransportRationalScalarLaw for every coefficient inclusion E≤L. Then IsomorphismFieldTransportCommon(l,Ω,g,hX,hY,S) is inhabited. The conclusion consists only of descent to the actual common-stage category: the exact additive equivalence, specified quotient-arrow formulas, identity-normalized stage/shift comparison, and epsilon represented by S_E's rational epsilon at the object's own stage. It assumes, and does not construct, all finite stages and their rational inverse/scalar equations.

source.place: First paragraph, inverse automorphism squares and “Since g* is an equivalence”; expanded steps of lem-pod-isomorphism-field-transport.

proof.text: Identify the actual commonStageDerivedPullback with its normalized stage-system morphism using commonStagePullback_comparison_data and the unique representative characterization. Its generic inclusion comparison has identity components, giving the required stageComparison.

Apply normalized shift descent to the supplied finite packages and this inclusion comparison. A distinguished triangle is isomorphic to an included finite-stage distinguished triangle. The shift-compatible stage comparison and finite rational exactness show that its pullback is distinguished, including the connecting map. Thus the chosen functor is triangulated and hence additive.

Construct each inverse component by transporting the inclusion of the supplied own-stage rational epsilon along the actual object equalities of the two chosen pullbacks. Epsilon naturality assembles these components into a natural isomorphism. Repeat for inv g using R and hR; inv(inv g)=g gives the other composite. Equivalence.mk yields equivalence. Retain the original epsilon so that its exact prescribed component formula is preserved.
Fill the object_formula and arrow_formula directly from commonStageDerivedPullback_existsUnique. Package these with the constructed comparison, shift, exactness, additivity, equivalence and epsilon.
